prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-28. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.68 |
| Retained earnings       | 24,804M |
| Current liabilities     | 9,335M |
| Current assets          | 6,320M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 31,173M |
| Total liabilities       | 24,587M |
| Total assets            | 60,792M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,002M |
| Revenue                 | 4,171M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-28, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The current ratio of 0.68 signals acute liquidity pressure and an inability to cover near-term obligations from liquid assets, outweighing the otherwise adequate leverage (liabilities/assets ~40%) and positive retained earnings. High margins do not offset the refinancing or asset-sale risk this creates. The profile is therefore consistent with upper speculative-grade credit quality.
DECISION: BB+
